title: F2FS Getting Ready With Its Large Folios Support
extract: Linux's F2FS filesystem is preparing support for large folios in buffered I/O, allowing it to handle multi-page memory units rather than single pages. Early benchmark results show substantial throughput improvements for some workloads, and the work is progressing in the filesystem's development branch for a possible Linux 7.5 release.

title: Intel Xe Driver Gaining PCIe Function Level Reset Support With Linux 7.5
extract: Intel's Xe graphics driver is gaining PCIe Function Level Reset support, allowing an individual PCIe function to be reset without disturbing other devices. The initial implementation is limited to reinitialising the GPU's graphics tile, with further components expected in follow-up work; it is useful groundwork for virtualization and targeted recovery.

title: KosmicKrisp Becomes the Go-To Vulkan Solution on Macs, Superseding MoltenVK
extract: The Khronos Group is deprecating its Vulkan Portability Initiative after LunarG's KosmicKrisp achieved Vulkan 1.4 conformance on Apple Silicon. Built into Mesa and layered over Metal, KosmicKrisp becomes the preferred route for modern Apple devices, while MoltenVK remains useful for older Intel Macs and older macOS versions.

title: GNU Linux-Libre Welcomes Reverse-Engineered Firmware for an Old VIA Wi-Fi Chipset
extract: A developer has reverse-engineered the firmware for VIA's VT6656 USB 802.11b/g adapter, allowing the driver to meet GNU Linux-libre's requirement for fully free firmware. The chipset is two decades old and its driver was removed from mainline Linux, but the work restores a free-software option for the older 6.12 LTS kernel.

title: Linux 7.5 to Whitelist Intel Xeon CPUs for Peer-to-Peer DMA
extract: Linux 7.5 is set to explicitly whitelist Intel Xeon server generations from Skylake-SP through Diamond Rapids for PCIe peer-to-peer DMA. This fixes cases in VMware and Hyper-V guests where passthrough devices lack the host-bridge information required by the existing checks, enabling direct transfers between GPUs, NICs and NVMe devices without routing data through system RAM.

title: 3mdeb Updates Coreboot-Based Dasharo Firmware for MSI Z690 and Z790 Motherboards
extract: 3mdeb has released updated Dasharo firmware builds for MSI PRO Z690-A and Z790-P motherboards. The updates improve experimental overclocking, DDR4 XMP training and CPU tuning, add USB power and wake controls, and enable Secure Boot, SMM write protection and early-boot IOMMU DMA protection by default.

title: Servo 0.8 Adds HTML Video Captions and Fixes Flutter Web Performance
extract: The Rust-based Servo browser engine now supports subtitles and captions in HTML5 video and works properly with Flutter web content after a typed-arrays performance fix. Servo 0.8 also brings CSS and Web API improvements, smoother zooming, lower memory use, fewer allocations and continued progress on WebGL2 and WebGPU.

title: Collabora Online Cuts Per-Document Memory Use by Around Half
extract: An optimization to Collabora Online's copy-on-write memory handling reduces memory use per open document by roughly 50%. The change addresses waste caused by 4KB kernel-page granularity when many small allocations are created and discarded during document startup, improving the efficiency of multi-user office deployments.

title: Alien Arena Arrives on Flathub With Gameplay and Networking Optimizations
extract: The open-source sci-fi first-person shooter Alien Arena is now available through Flathub for x86-64 and AArch64 Linux systems. Version 7.72.4 brings movement and strafing improvements, better lag compensation, dynamic culling, bot behaviour changes, networking fixes and graphical refinements.

title: Linux 7.4 Disables LLVM Profi to Avoid Slower Binaries and Pathological Build Times
extract: The Linux 7.4 kernel is disabling LLVM's Profi flow-based profile inference when AutoFDO is used. Interactions with the kernel's flow-sensitive discriminators could make optimized binaries slower and trigger extremely long or stalled compilation, so the change is also being prepared for stable-kernel backports.

title: TornadoVM 8.2 Adds a Native AMD ROCm HIP Backend for Java GPU Computing
extract: TornadoVM 8.2 adds a dedicated ROCm HIP backend to its Java framework for JIT-compiling workloads to GPUs. The new backend interfaces directly with the HIP runtime on Windows and Linux, alongside continued improvements to Apple Metal support and updates for OpenJ9 and IBM Semeru.

title: PostgreSQL 19 Shows Promising Gains on AMD's 6th-Generation EPYC Venice
extract: Initial Phoronix benchmarks compare PostgreSQL 19 with version 18 on a 256-core AMD EPYC 9996 Venice server. Improvements from asynchronous I/O workers, SIMD acceleration, faster foreign-key checks and parallel autovacuum deliver measurable gains without changing the database configuration.

title: Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS Released With More COSMIC Apps and Remote Desktop
extract: System76 has released Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS, based on Ubuntu 26.04 LTS and the latest COSMIC desktop. New features include automatic updates, COSMIC System Monitor and Store applications, drawing-tablet support, remote desktop, improved magnification and better hybrid-GPU handling.

title: Linus Torvalds Criticizes a Huge AI-Assisted EXT4 Pull Request During the Linux 7.4 Cycle
extract: Linus Torvalds accepted a large EXT4 pull request containing more than 41,000 lines, but sharply criticized its timing and the volume of AI-generated fixes arriving late in the Linux 7.4 release cycle. He stressed that AI-assisted patches still need disciplined review, testing and separate development branches.

title: Ubuntu Outlines an Optional, Local-First AI Interface for the Desktop
extract: Canonical has shared more detail on an experimental Ubuntu desktop launcher intended to connect files, applications and local context through keyboard- and speech-friendly interaction. The proposed assistant is opt-in, local-first and privacy-focused; the current warty-prototype Snap is a design mock-up, with architecture details planned for January.

title: Benchmarking Shows Linux FRED Support Can Improve I/O Performance on AMD Zen 6
extract: Phoronix has measured the effect of Flexible Return and Event Delivery on AMD's EPYC 9006 Zen 6 processors by comparing Linux 7.4 with FRED disabled. The newer interrupt and exception mechanism delivered gains of a few percent in some networking and local-storage tests, complementing other Zen 6 platform improvements.

title: Porsche Creates a One-Off 911 GT3 Tribute to the 911 GT1
extract: Porsche China has commissioned a one-off 911 GT3 in a hand-painted livery inspired by the 1996 911 GT1, marking 30 years of the race car and Zhuhai International Circuit. The road car retains the naturally aspirated 4.0-litre flat-six, producing 510 PS and revving to 9,000 rpm, with bespoke Sonderwunsch details throughout.

title: The Hobbit – Amiga AGA Enhanced Edition Brings the Classic Adventure to the A1200
extract: Developer thall72 has ported the MSX version of Melbourne House's 1982 The Hobbit to native 68000 code for AGA-equipped Amigas. The release keeps the original parser, puzzles and independent characters while adding more than 60 new 256-colour paintings, an AGA intro, rearranged C64 music, disk saving and a WHDLoad edition; it has been tested on real A1200 hardware, MiSTer and emulators.

title: Blade Runner 2099 Premieres on Prime Video as an Eight-Episode Limited Series
extract: Blade Runner 2099 arrives on Prime Video as an eight-episode binge release, with Michelle Yeoh leading the dystopian sequel set decades after Blade Runner 2049 and Hunter Schafer co-starring. The series explores a future Los Angeles shaped by artificial humans known as replicants.
